# Shared memory

`v1/memory` — one memory every agent shares, whatever its CLI, read and written through geniro's own tools (`memory_search`, `memory_read`, `memory_save`, `memory_forget`, `memory_feedback`; base `MemoryMcpTool`, `.claude/rules/mcp-tools.md`).

- `memories` rows are teardown-exempt (root `AGENTS.md` → *Storage split*); provenance (`sourceActor`, `sourceAgentKind`, `sourceModel`, `sourceRunId`) is a plain copy, never a foreign key. `memories_fts` is the second recorded FTS exception (`.claude/rules/database-queries.md`), repaired at boot by `MemoryTextIndexService.ensure()` beside the chat index.
- Every write goes through `MemoryService.save` / `forget` with a `MemoryActor`, serialized so a handle (`m<n>`, one past the highest, never reused) and the near-duplicate check see a table no other write is changing. The service, not the approval, holds the limits: one-line title ≤ `MEMORY_TITLE_MAX_CHARS`, body ≤ `MEMORY_BODY_MAX_BYTES` (8 KB, so the CLIs' own notes import — user decision), refusal when `redactSecrets` would change the text (registered secrets only — an unregistered key is not caught, accepted), a near-duplicate title in the target scope (word overlap over FTS candidates; `notDuplicateOf` vouches past it), and a stale `rev`.
- Review mode (`agentWrites: pending`, user decision): an agent's — or an analysis chat's — NEW entry lands `pending`, and its update or forget of an existing entry is refused `UNDER_REVIEW`, so reviewed text is never replaced unseen. A near-duplicate refusal quotes only `active` entries; a match among `pending` ones is named by handle (`near_duplicate.pending`), never quoted, and blocks only an agent — the user is the reviewer. `notDuplicateOf` vouches past either. A forget keeps the writer's provenance. `setStatus` (approve, restore, forget) takes an actor and refuses an agent (`USER_ONLY`). Forgetting records what the entry was (`statusBeforeForget`) and keeps its `approvedAt`; a restore puts it back there, so a pending entry waits for review again and only an Approve press approves (user decision).
- Only `active` entries are searched or read by an agent; `pending` waits for the user's review and `forgotten` is restorable. An agent sees global entries plus its run's project's and, in a team run, its team's (`Memory.teamSlug`; each entry is filed in exactly one of global, project or team — `RunPlace`). Every tool result is masked with `redactSecrets` (a secret registered after an entry was saved never leaves), and a whole body is quoted inside a fence with a random name per reply, so a body cannot forge another entry's header.
- A team entry is keyed by its slug. Deleting a team settles its entries as the user chose in the delete dialog (`TeamChatService.deleteTeam` → `MemoryService.settleDeletedTeam`: `forget` restorably, `keep` under the slug, which a later team of that name reads, or `global`). The user's create and edit refuse a slug the library does not hold (`NO_TEAM`, through the lookup `TeamChatService` registers with `useTeamLookup`, since `v1/memory` may not import `v1/teams`); an entry kept under a deleted team's slug can still be edited where it stands.
- The place is the daemon's (`MemoryService.scopeOf`, a `RunPlace`): the team is the run's `teamId` (null for chats, analyses and builder chats); the project is the one settled when the run was created (`Run.projectId` / `Run.projectSource`, read live, so a deleted project means global only); a run from before that was recorded keeps the old rule — its task card's project, else the live project bound to exactly the folder `ProjectRootsService.rootsOf` resolves the run's folder to. The caller is `actorOf`: a team node's own `NodeState` agent and model, else the run's; an analysis run writes as `analysis`. Known limit: a pooled node's member that took over is recorded as member 1 (`node_state` holds member 1's agent).
- Reading stamps `lastUsedAt` through the builder, never a flush (a flush would move `updatedAt`).
- Usage is counted per entry and per UTC day in `memory_usage_days` (`reads`, `searchHits`, `indexShows`; key `(memoryId, day)`), only by increments (`MemoryUsageDao.add`, an insert that adds onto the existing row). `MemoryUsageService` counts live: a `memory_read` that returned the entry (a missing handle counts nothing; only a read is a use, and it alone moves `lastUsedAt`), each `memory_search` hit, and each entry a new run's index lists (`MemoryRunSnapshot.indexIds`, counted by the two Run builders once the row exists and never stored on it — `runSnapshot` also measures instruction sizes for no run). A failed count, or a failed `lastUsedAt` stamp, is logged and never reaches the tool answer or the run start.
- The usage before the ledger existed is backfilled once from the only place it is still recorded, the stored memory calls (`items`) and `Run.memoryIndex`, by `MemoryUsageBackfillService`, chained after the payload-column sweep off the ready path. Live counting starts only after a cutoff is durable in `<userData>/memory-usage-backfill` (JSON `{cutoff, doneVersion}`, taken at the first launch with the ledger, before listen); the backfill counts only rows created before it, so no use is counted twice. Calls are found by their stored names (claude's `mcp__geniro-<run8>__<tool>`, cursor's `geniro-<run8>: <tool>`; any other spelling counts nothing) and paired with their results as `pairToolCalls` pairs them. A read's entries are its result's entry headers, read outside the fenced bodies (`utils/memory-usage-history.ts`, twin of the readers' text); cursor's results carry no text, so its reads count the handles asked for and its searches count nothing. Each run's counts and its `memory_usage_backfill` row commit together; a run whose payload columns are not stamped yet, or that failed, is passed over and keeps the pass running at the next launch, and the marker's `doneVersion` retires it once every run is counted (`MEMORY_USAGE_BACKFILL_VERSION`).
- A new run snapshots the memory once, in the two Run builders (`createChat`, the executor's `startRun`), before its row exists: `MemoryService.runSnapshot` over `scopeFor` with the project `ProjectScopeService.placeNewRun` settled for the same run (`placedFacts`), so the memory index and the project instructions follow one answer, writes `Run.memoryIndex` and `Run.nativeMemoryOff`, and every turn reads both off the row like `customInstructions`, since both join `sessionKey` — a note saved or the switch flipped mid-run restarts nothing and reaches the next run. Until Electron's first push it snapshots nothing (the default is not the user's choice). A failed read starts the run without an index, never refuses it.
- The index (`memoryIndexOf`) lists only entries the user wrote or imported, or approved by hand (`Memory.approvedAt`, stamped by the user's `setStatus` to `active` or `setIndexed` (`POST /v1/memories/:id/index`), cleared by `/search-only` and by any later save), or an auto lesson promoted by agents' marks (`Memory.promotedAt`, cleared by an agent's rewrite like `approvedAt`; the user's `/search-only` on a lesson clears it and stamps `restoredAt`, so only marks given after that count toward promoting it again): an agent's unreviewed entry is reached only through `memory_search` (user decision, after research: a note an agent was steered into saving must not speak in every later run's instructions; user decision 2026-11-15: kept, with the UI splitting entries into In every chat / Search only). `MemoryEntry.indexed` carries the rule to clients and `GET /v1/memories?reach=index|search` filters by it (`indexable` in the service and `reachExpression` in the DAO are twins); `GET /v1/memories/index-preview` cuts a place's index exactly as `runSnapshot` does and answers how many titles fit of how many eligible. Active entries the run may see, its team's first, then its project's, most recently used first, one line each (handle, type, masked title, scope, last use), cut on whole lines at `MEMORY_INDEX_MAX_BYTES` with a `+N more` footer; null when empty or memory is off.
- Each CLI's own memory can be switched off per run (`Run.nativeMemoryOff` → `AgentTurnInput.nativeMemoryOff`): claude through `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY` in its env, codex through `features.memories = false` in every thread config (endpoint or not); cursor-agent keeps none. Each switch is measured beside its constant. `runSnapshot` sets it only while the shared memory is on and the user switched the CLIs' own memory off (`MemoryConfig.nativeMemoryOff`, off by default and turned on by a successful import in Settings → Memory — user decision, so the CLIs' notes are never hidden before they are brought over).
- Settings arrive by push only (`PUT /v1/memories/config`, desktop only, `MemoryConfigSchema`: the UI's `memorySchema` plus `autoForgetAfterDays` from the top-level `memoryAutoForgetAfterDays`); until the first push the daemon holds `DEFAULT_MEMORY_CONFIG` (on, writes active) — the kept-session pattern, not the share one. Off removes the tools from every listing and refuses a kept CLI's call `MEMORY_DISABLED`. A run's prompt prefix never moves with the memory: entries saved, edited, approved or imported reach only new runs' instructions, and the review policy (read at each write) and the CLIs'-own-memory switch leave it as it is (the index and `nativeMemoryOff` are the run's snapshot, and the tools' descriptions are fixed text). Only the on/off switch itself moves it — no `list_changed` is sent, so a live CLI keeps the list it was spawned with, and a process of an existing run spawned after the switch lists the tools anew, costing that thread its prompt cache once (user decision: accepted rather than freezing the tool set per run).
- Auto-approved in a chat (`autoApproves`, in-turn and between turns) and in a team member at every approval level, in-turn and between turns (`isHostMemoryCall`, the executor's one host-tool approval), because a card per search would make memory unusable; every entry keeps who wrote it, and the user sees every entry in Settings → Memory.
- Each write publishes `memory_changed` (`MemoryEventBus`) to EVERY client, paired devices included (the user reads and edits memory from the phone); the event names the entry (`memoryId` null for a `bulk` change: forget-all, an import, a purge, a cleanup batch and its undo, the last two carrying `batchId`) and what the write did (`created`, `updated`, `forgotten`, `restored`, `approved`, `bulk`), never its text.
- The user's own routes (`MemoriesController`, `/v1/memories`) are open to paired devices (user decision); the config push (`MemoryConfigController`), the purge (`MemoryPurgeController`), the import (`MemoryImportController`) and the cleanup's model check (`MemoryCheckController`) are desktop only, each its own class because `DesktopOnlyGuard` sits on the class. A user's edit (`MemoryService.edit`, by id at the `rev` it read) makes the entry the user's own — a pending agent entry edited by the user is active and no longer waits on review; a forgotten one must be restored before it is edited. A near-duplicate refusal is `409 MEMORY_NEAR_DUPLICATE` whose message lists the handles (`NEAR_DUPLICATE_PREFIX`, twin of the renderer's `nearDuplicateHandles` in `components/use-memory-editor.ts`), so the pane vouches past exactly those. Forget-all is one statement over `active` and `pending` (each stays restorable); export is every active and pending entry as Markdown (`utils/memory-export.ts`).
- Import (`MemoryImportService`, in `v1/agents` because it walks `AgentAdapterRegistry`; its routes are `MemoryImportController`, desktop only): it only READS each CLI's own memory, through the adapter hook `readNativeMemory(configDir | null)` (null = the CLI's default profile; a CLI that keeps none answers null) and `nativeMemoryProjectKey(folder)` — claude's `<profile>/projects/*/memory/*.md` (not `MEMORY.md`), codex's `memories/MEMORY.md` task groups, never a symlinked directory or file, never codex's `memories_1.sqlite`. It never writes, moves or deletes a file there. Every profile the renderer names is read beside each CLI's default. A note's project is the live project whose key matches; two projects claiming one key leave it Global (`ambiguous`). A preview key names the note's text (a hash of title and body), so apply re-reads the files and skips a note edited or rewritten since the preview instead of storing text nobody saw; a second copy of one note (`sameAs`) and a key ticked twice are written once. Ticking a note is the user's review (user decision): imported entries land active with `approvedAt` stamped, in one flush, announced as one `bulk` change. Each row names its `profile` and the `folder` the note was written for (claude: read from a session filed beside the note, kept only when it flattens back to that directory; codex: none), home shown as `~`. The AI sort (`POST /v1/memories/import/triage`, `MemoryImportService.triage`) is advice only: it writes nothing, takes the notes' text from the client, masks it (`redactSecrets`) and puts one batch to the chosen CLI through `AgentAdapter.askOnce` (a throwaway turn isolated like the title ask; the model, effort, context window, model parameters and profile are the user's pick, checked as a chat's are by `OneShotAskService` — `EffortsService.accepts`, the CLI's `configDir.unavailableReason`, `resolveValidConfigDir` — and the cheap model at low effort on the default profile when none is picked; `AdapterConfig.oneShotAskUnavailableReason` says which CLIs cannot, served as the preview's `triageAgents`); the prompt and its reader are `utils/memory-triage.ts`, and a note the answer skipped simply has no verdict.
- Cleanup (`MemoryReviewService` reads, `MemoryService.forgetBatch` / `restoreBatch` / `setKept` writes; routes on `MemoriesController`, open to paired devices). Least used is cold rows only: active or pending, not kept (`keptAt`, the user's only protection — user decision), no ledger read in `MEMORY_COLD_DAYS` and `lastUsedAt` older or null, at least `minAgeDays` old (default `MEMORY_REVIEW_MIN_AGE_DAYS`); every sort, filter, count and page is one Kysely read over `memories` joined to the ledger summed per entry (`MemoryDao.review`), never folded from a page. A row is warned when its type is `feedback` or `user`, the user wrote it, or `statesRule` is true or still null (`warnedExpression`, twin `warningOf`); the warning never hides a row, only keeps it out of `review/ids` (Tick shown). `statesRule` and `referencedPaths` are read from the text on every save and import (`utils/memory-references.ts`: a limit word in the title or first 200 body characters, English and Russian; repo-relative file paths, never a URL, absolute, home or `..` path) and for older rows by `sweepQuietly`, after the usage backfill off the ready path. `referencesGone` is checked against the project's folder when the list's first page is read and the last check is over an hour old (`refreshReferences`, single-flight): only `ENOENT`/`ENOTDIR` is gone, a denied folder is present and a missing project root leaves the entry unjudged.
- Every forget path stamps `forgottenAt` and clears `forgetBatchId` (`utils/memory-forget-stamp.ts`: `forgetNow`, `applyStatus`, `forgetAll`, `forgetTeam`), a batch stamps its own id, and every restore clears both and stamps `restoredAt`; so a batch's undo (`status = forgotten AND forget_batch_id = :id`) never brings back a row restored or forgotten again by hand, and each row returns to its own `statusBeforeForget`, pending included. Batches, Keep, the sweep and the reference check write through the builder without `updated_at`, so the user's list keeps its order. A batch is announced as one `bulk` `memory_changed` carrying `batchId`. `GET /v1/memories/batches` groups the still-forgotten rows by batch id, so an undone batch drops out. The import preview marks a note whose text a forgotten or purged imported entry held (`forgottenEarlier`, `forgottenImportedHashes`: `importedTextHash` of the forgotten rows plus the purged rows' `purgedTextHash`, read past the soft-delete filter); apply's `importedTexts` stays active and pending only, so a ticked one imports again.
- The check for duplicates and contradictions (user decision: one-shot questions on a press, never a chat analysis; the user decides every pair). `MemoryFindingsService` (`v1/memory`) finds likely pairs with no model: each active entry's rarest words (rarity counted over every active entry read in yielding windows, `utils/memory-pairs.ts`) searched in `memories_fts`, its top `MEMORY_CHECK_PARTNERS` partners among entries some run sees beside it (a global entry with anything, two of one project or one team; two projects never meet). `MemoryCheckService` (`v1/agents`, `MemoryCheckController`, desktop only: it runs the Mac's CLI, billed to the user's account) answers `GET /v1/memories/review/pairs` with the pairs, a token estimate (`approxInstructionTokens`) and a cost at the picked model's list price (`billingRatesOf`, null = not measured), and `POST /v1/memories/review/check` asks one batch of at most `MEMORY_CHECK_PAIRS_MAX` through `OneShotAskService` — the one place a one-shot memory question checks its CLI, profile and effort, which the import's Sort with AI uses too. The prompt (`utils/memory-check-prompt.ts`) opens with `MEMORY_NOTES_FRAMING` (`askOnce` withholds only geniro's tools, so the text is framed as data), sends whole bodies masked by `redactSecrets`, asks `duplicate | supersedes | contradicts | conditional | unrelated` with a verbatim quote from each entry, and forbids inferring a conflict from recency. A finding stands only when both quotes are found in the masked text sent (whitespace runs as one); otherwise it is stored as `unquoted` and never shown. One row per pair in `memory_review_findings` (exempt from run teardown) pins both texts by hash (`memoryTextHash`), not `rev`, which a forget or restore moves: a pair checked is not offered again, and a finding not shown, until either text changes. `GET /v1/memories/review/findings` and `POST .../findings/:findingId/dismiss` ("Both are true") are open to paired devices; a finding shows while both entries are active at the hashed texts and it is not dismissed, so an undone Keep or merge brings it back while a dismissal stays. Stop is the client's: the batch already asked runs on, billed, up to the CLI's ask timeout. Every marker of the prompt carries a tag drawn per question, so a note's own text cannot close its block or forge another pair. A purge deletes the findings naming the entry (see Purge).
- Merge (`MemoryService.merge`, `POST /v1/memories/merge`, open to paired devices): in one serialized transaction it writes a new entry as the user (the user saw and edited the whole text, so it is indexable like any of theirs) and forgets the sources through `forgetBatch` with one `forgetBatchId` and `mergedIntoId`; any outcome but `created` — a near-duplicate of a third entry included — throws inside the transaction, so nothing is forgotten, and events publish after the commit. Restoring the batch also forgets the entry the merge wrote (found through its sources' `mergedIntoId`); every restore clears `mergedIntoId`, so a source restored by hand stops adding to the merged entry's figures. `MemoryDao.review` credits a merged entry with the ledger of every source still forgotten into it, each source keeping its own.
- Purge (`MemoryService.purge`, `POST /v1/memories/:memoryId/purge` on `MemoryPurgeController`, desktop only): only a `forgotten` row (`400 MEMORY_NOT_FORGOTTEN` otherwise). It is a tombstone written through the builder in one transaction: title, body and `forgetReason` emptied (the FTS update trigger drops the text from search), `forgetBatchId` cleared, `deletedAt` set and, for an imported entry only, `purgedTextHash`, `updated_at` untouched; the row keeps its handle (`nextHandle` reads past the soft-delete filter, so it is never reused), its provenance and its `memory_usage_days`. Every `memory_review_findings` row naming it, on either side of the pair, is deleted in the same transaction (`MemoryReviewFindingDao.deleteNaming`), so no quote of its text outlives it. Past transcripts keep what a tool showed.
- The automatic sweep (`MemoryService.sweepCold`, user decision: off by default, forget-only): armed by `MemoryConfig.autoForgetAfterDays` (the top-level settings key `memoryAutoForgetAfterDays`, desktop only), on a daemon-owned timer in `MemoryService` (5 minutes after start, then every 24 h, unref'd, cleared at shutdown, never on a push). It runs only after Electron's first push, while memory is on, with a window set and once the usage backfill is done (`doneVersion`), else every entry would look unread. It forgets, as one batch through the same path as `forgetBatch`, the `active` rows that are not kept and not warned whose `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `approvedAt`, `restoredAt`, `lastUsedAt` and last ledger read are all older than the window, filed in a scope with a new run in `MEMORY_DORMANT_SCOPE_DAYS` (any run for global, the run's `projectId` or `teamId` otherwise; `RunDao.placesWithRunsSince`). The one filter (`utils/memory-auto-forget.ts` → `MemoryDao.autoForgetIds` / `autoForgetCounts`) also answers `GET /v1/memories/review/summary?autoForgetDays=N` (`autoForget: {days, forget, warned}`), the figure the arm confirm names (marked provisional while the backfill is still counting). Its batch id opens with `MEMORY_AUTO_BATCH_PREFIX`, so `GET /v1/memories/batches` and the summary's `lastBatch` mark it `automatic`. It never purges and never asks a model.
- Marks (`memory_marks`, `MemoryMarkDao`, teardown-exempt; user decisions R7–R9): an agent's `memory_feedback` (`helped` | `not_useful` | `misleading`, a one-line reason ≤ `MEMORY_FEEDBACK_REASON_MAX_CHARS`, secret-checked; not offered to a hidden lessons chat by the allow-list, refused `REFLECTION_READ_ONLY` if reached) and a lessons reflection's `propose_lessons.effects` (`followed` → `helped`, `misled` → `misleading`, `broken` → `broken`). The thread is the run (every member of a team run votes as one; a reflection's or a thread analysis's mark counts for the thread it read, `analysisSourceRunId`), unique per `(memoryId, threadId, source)`, a later mark replacing the earlier. Only an entry the run had in front of it may be marked — in `Run.memoryIndex` or returned by its own `memory_read` (`MemoryMarksService.seenBy` over the stored calls, `runMemoryUsage`), else `NOT_SEEN`; a `helped` mark stamps `lastUsedAt` and, for an entry the run had only in its index, counts a read (one it read was counted by that `memory_read`). Allowed while the user reviews agent writes: a mark edits no entry.
- The fold (`utils/memory-marks-fold.ts`, over every mark of the last `MEMORY_MARKS_WINDOW_DAYS` newer than the entry's `restoredAt`, so a restore discards older marks): one vote per thread, its newest mark across sources, `misleading` counting as not useful, `broken` never counting. `MemoryService` acts on it after each mark and in `sweepMarks`, chained after the cold sweep on its timer: not useful − helped ≥ `MEMORY_MARKS_FORGET_THRESHOLD` forgets ANY active entry as its own `marks-` batch whose `forgetReason` names each thread's title and reason (`MemoryConfig.removeNotUseful`, the top-level settings key `memoryRemoveNotUseful`, on by default, stops this and its purge); an active auto lesson (`sourceActor: lesson`, neither approved nor promoted) with no `helped` mark for `MEMORY_LESSON_EXPIRY_DAYS` since its filing or restore is forgotten in one `expired-lesson-` batch; either rule's entries still forgotten `MEMORY_RULE_PURGE_AFTER_DAYS` later are purged (`purgeNow`, as the user's purge, which deletes the entry's marks with its text); an auto lesson `helped` by ≥ `MEMORY_PROMOTE_HELPED_THREADS` threads and not useful to none gets `promotedAt`. `MemoryEntry.forgetReason` and `purgeAt`, `MemoryForgetBatch.kind` / `title` / `reason` / `purgeAt` and `MemoryList.tracks` (index shows and reads over every ledger day, helped and not useful as the fold counts them) carry it to Settings.
- Module direction: `MemoryModule` imports only `ProjectsModule` (whose `ProjectScopeService` answers which project a run belongs to) and provides the run and node-state DAOs it reads, so `AgentsModule` and `TeamsModule` (the run snapshot), `McpModule` and `NotificationsModule` import it, never the reverse.
